record.paper_title: Complete intersection liaison and Gorenstein liaison: new results and open problems
record.original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let R = k[X0, ..., X_{n+3}] with irrelevant maximal ideal m, and let X be a closed arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay subscheme of P^{n+3} of dimension n > 0 and codimension 3. Let I = I(X), A = R/I, and K = Ext^3_R(A,R)(-n-4), the canonical module of X. A necessary condition for X to be licci is that the local cohomology groups H^i_m(K tensor_R I) vanish for all 0 <= i <= n. Is the converse true: whenever H^i_m(K tensor_R I) = 0 for every i with 0 <= i <= n, must X be licci, meaning in the complete-intersection liaison class of a complete intersection?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, let $R = k[X_0, X_1, \ldots, X_{n+3}]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring with irrelevant maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m} = (X_0, \ldots, X_{n+3})$, and let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+3}_k$ be a closed arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay subscheme of dimension $n > 0$ and codimension $3$. Set $I = I(X) \subset R$, $A = R/I$, and let 
$$K = \mathrm{Ext}^{3}_{R}(A, R)(-n-4)$$
be the (graded) canonical module of $X$. Recall that $X$ (equivalently, $I$) is called licci if it lies in the complete-intersection liaison class of a complete intersection, i.e., it can be linked to a complete intersection in finitely many steps via complete-intersection links. It is known that if $X$ is licci, then the graded local cohomology modules satisfy
$$H^{i}_{\mathfrak{m}}(K \otimes_{R} I) = 0 \quad \text{for all } 0 \le i \le n.$$
Question: Is the converse true? That is, if $X$ is an arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^{n+3}$ of dimension $n>0$ and codimension $3$ such that $H^{i}_{\mathfrak{m}}(K \otimes_{R} I) = 0$ for every $0 \le i \le n$, must $X$ be licci?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return a definitive proof or disproof of the converse direction of this licci criterion in codimension 3. Related work (Huneke-Ulrich on linkage and residual intersections, and recent studies of licci monomial/Stanley-Reisner ideals of height 3) addresses the necessary condition and special cases, but no source clearly establishes the converse in full generality. The status appears to remain unresolved.
